# Run a product beta or design-partner program

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before broad release when a product needs controlled validation with selected users. A reviewed beta outcome with user feedback, operational readiness and an explicit launch or further-test decision.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Define the learning goals and eligibility

agent-runnable


State the product behavior to test, target users, known limitations and evidence needed for a decision. Identify data sensitivity and risks that would make a participant or use case unsuitable.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Approve the participant terms and safeguards

human · human approval required


Product, security and legal owners review beta access, support, confidentiality, data handling and exit arrangements. Confirm that participation does not imply production readiness or permission for an otherwise regulated use.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Provision the approved beta environment

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


Invite only approved participants and configure limited access, monitoring and recovery. Test onboarding and support routes and record the software version and features each cohort receives.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Collect feedback and operating evidence

agent-runnable


Track adoption, task success, defects, incidents and qualitative feedback against the learning goals. Maintain a reproducible issue register while minimizing personal data in reports.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Decide whether to launch, extend or stop

human · human approval required


The accountable owners review the evidence, unresolved risks and support capacity. Communicate the approved decision, migrate or remove beta access appropriately and hand launch work to the release process.

- Verify: A reviewed beta outcome with user feedback, operational readiness and an explicit launch or further-test decision.
- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/) · [NIST Secure Software Development Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf)
